text:
Maya: Quick idea  add an "allow-costly-fallbacks" checkbox in the operator panel. If unchecked, the UI blocks any action that would exceed a configured safety leash. Proto/mock here: https://figma.com/proto/allow-costly-fallbacks
Rohit: Love the gating. We should also make it clear in the API: is the guard enforced client-side only or server-side? Must be server-side for org-level safety.
Sam: Server-side enforce for sure. Also propose a secondary "cost-confirmation" modal when the action would use >5% of monthly safety pool. Shows estimated tokens and USD.
Leia: Telemetry: emit structured event `fallback_confirmation_v1` with fields: decision_id, actor, pre_weight, post_weight, est_tokens, est_usd, allowed_by_checkbox (bool), safety_pool_scope (route|org). Retain 90d and exportable.
Tomas: API debate: do we standardize on header `X-Fallback-Decision` (uuid) or `X-Fallback-Change-Id`? Decision implies intent, change implies action. Prefer `X-Fallback-Decision` because decision_token attaches to both simulated and applied actions.
Maya: Good point. We also need a field in the decision record: "allowed_by_checkbox" vs "bypassed_by_admin" for audit clarity.
Rohit: RBAC nuance: allow junior ops to see the checkbox but not check it. It should be disabled with tooltip "requires senior approval". That prevents accidental cost hits.
Sam: UX note: if checkbox disabled, include a one-click "request approval" flow that pings oncall and creates a temporary approval token valid for N minutes. Approval actions are logged.
Leia: For redaction: sampled request/response snapshots attached to decisions must strip user-provided content and only keep hashed user IDs. Export pipeline must run the redactor before BigQuery write.
Tomas: Implementation: decision_token (uuid) created at UI start, stored in decisions table. If operator checks checkbox, we mark decision.allowed=true and attach actor. Header `X-Fallback-Decision: <uuid>` flows with requests for trace joins. I'll add `allowed_by_checkbox` boolean to proto.

ops-bot: ops-bot: nightly check: canary completed, no fallbacks triggered on chat-route

Maya: One more: add a small "safety-preview" line under the action button that shows "this will use ~0.8% of org fallback pool" and links to breakdown. Helps reduce modal friction.

Rohit: Also add an audit-only dry-run where checkbox can be toggled but action not applied; marks decision.preview=true. Useful for runbooks.

Sam: Agree. Default action when triggered by automatic policy should not auto-check the box; operator must explicitly enable to allow costly steps.

Leia: I'll write the retention/export spec: decisions 90d, sampled payloads 30d, BigQuery export daily, redaction pipeline mandatory.

Tomas: I'll update the proto snippet and push telemetry PR: message FallbackDecision { string decision_id = 1; string route = 2; string action = 3; bool allowed_by_checkbox = 4; string decision_token = 5; map<string,string> meta = 6; }

Maya: Great. I'll add the checkbox to the mock and the approval flow. Thanks all.
